milestones.title: Midwest Research Institute (MRI) Beverage Container Resource & Environmental Profile Study
milestones.actor: Midwest Research Institute (commissioned by The Coca-Cola Company)
milestones.summary: First systematic cradle-to-grave tracking of energy, raw material, and waste ledgers across glass bottles, metal cans, and plastic beverage containers.
milestones.significance: Widely recognized as the origin of modern life cycle inventory (LCI), shifting packaging debates from single stages to full-chain material and energy balances.
milestones.pendingNote: The 1969 internal MRI report commissioned by Coca-Cola was never released publicly in full. This book directly inspects the same team’s 1974 public report, EPA SW-91c (see the 1974 milestone), while details specific to the 1969 internal study draw on subsequent public accounts.

milestones.title: Research Triangle Institute (RTI) Beverage Container Policy Report
milestones.summary: Introduced systematic comparisons of refillable and single-use containers into energy and solid-waste policy debates, showing how trip rates, recycling rates, and transport distances overturn policy rankings.
milestones.significance: First clear demonstration that identical physical ledgers can yield opposite policy conclusions under different use-behavior assumptions.

milestones.title: US EPA Resource and Environmental Profile Analysis (REPA) Report
milestones.summary: Published the resource and environmental profile methodology and data boundaries for nine beverage container systems, establishing the early REPA inventory paradigm.
milestones.significance: Moved life cycle accounting from proprietary corporate commissions into public government reports and auditable methodological texts.

milestones.title: Swiss Federal Office for Environmental Protection (BUS) Packaging Ecobalance & Critical Volume Method
milestones.actor: Swiss Federal Office for Environmental Protection (BUS)
milestones.summary: Systematically compiled European packaging inventory data and introduced 'critical volumes' scaled to regulatory emission limits, paving the way for the Ecological Scarcity (UBP) method.
milestones.significance: Marked Europe's transition from pure mass-and-energy ledgers toward impact aggregation anchored in environmental carrying capacity and policy targets.
milestones.pendingNote: The original 1984 German-language BUS Report No. 24 is not available in full online and is summarized here from subsequent public literature; see Ecological Scarcity Weighting for directly inspected later sources on the method.

milestones.title: SETAC Vermont Workshop Establishes 'Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)' Terminology
milestones.actor: Society of Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry (SETAC)
milestones.summary: Convened European and North American researchers to standardize the name Life Cycle Assessment and define its three-component technical framework: inventory, impact assessment, and improvement analysis.
milestones.significance: Elevated LCA from scattered packaging energy studies into an internationally coordinated methodological discipline.
milestones.pendingNote: The original 1990 SETAC Vermont workshop report (Fava et al., 1991) is not publicly available in full; this entry relies on 1992–1996 public guidance documents.

milestones.title: CML Guide to Environmental Life Cycle Assessment of Products (CML 1992)
milestones.actor: Heijungs et al. (Centre of Environmental Science, Leiden University)
milestones.summary: Constructed the classification–characterization–normalization–valuation midpoint LCIA sequence and formalized process inventory calculation via linear algebra matrices.
milestones.significance: Laid the twin theoretical foundations of modern midpoint LCIA and matrix-based inventory solving.

milestones.title: US EPA Life-Cycle Assessment: Inventory Guidelines and Principles & Contemporary Codes
milestones.actor: US EPA (parallel with SETAC 1993 Code of Practice)
milestones.summary: Codified goal and scope definition, functional units, data quality documentation, boundary cut-off rules, peer review, and transparency requirements.
milestones.significance: Translated the principle of 'define the service function before building the process ledger' into an operational engineering handbook.
milestones.verificationNote: Directly based on the original US EPA 1993 report (EPA/600/R-92/245); the contemporaneous SETAC 1993 Code of Practice is drawn from subsequent public guidance.

milestones.title: First Edition of ISO 14040 Establishes the Modern Four-Phase Framework
milestones.summary: Replaced early 'improvement analysis' with iterative 'life cycle interpretation' spanning goal and scope definition, inventory analysis, impact assessment, and interpretation.
milestones.significance: Became the first global international standard skeleton for LCA, followed by ISO 14041, 14042, and 14043.
milestones.pendingNote: ISO 14040:1997 is a withdrawn paywalled standard whose full text has not been consulted; its historical role is drawn from the CML 2001 and US EPA 2006 public guides.

chapters.label: Life Cycle Assessment in Cleaner Production

milestones.title: Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) Electricity Trade Balance Models & Marginal Debate
milestones.summary: Constructed M1–M4 physical electricity allocation models from 1995 Swiss customs and generation statistics while explicitly documenting the 'average mix vs. marginal supply' disagreement in footnotes.
milestones.significance: First rigorous empirical demonstration that the same kilowatt-hour of purchased electricity maps to different generation sources depending on accounting boundaries.

milestones.title: Weidema Proposes Consequential System Expansion & Constrained-Market Identification
milestones.summary: Introduced a stepwise procedure using market boundaries, capacity trends, and supply constraints to identify marginal suppliers affected by demand changes, establishing consequential LCA.
milestones.significance: Drew a sharp boundary between attributional accounting (who shares existing burdens) and consequential modeling (whose output changes in response to demand).

milestones.title: CML 2001/2002 Handbook on Life Cycle Assessment Published
milestones.summary: Organized midpoint characterization factors into simplified, baseline, and extended tiers, strongly recommended normalization, and reaffirmed the prohibition on weighting in comparative assertions disclosed to the public.
milestones.significance: Established one of the most widely cited midpoint baseline characterization systems across academia and industry for two decades.

milestones.title: Suh et al. Systematize Tiered, Input-Output-Based, and Integrated Hybrid LCI
milestones.summary: Quantified system boundary truncation errors in pure process inventories, closed upstream gaps with environmentally extended input-output (EEIO) tables, and formulated double-counting subtraction rules.
milestones.significance: Brought the fundamental trade-off between process truncation error and sector aggregation/price-conversion error to center stage.

milestones.title: Japan's LIME Damage-Oriented LCIA & Monetized Valuation Framework
milestones.summary: Used conjoint analysis preference surveys to derive monetized weighting factors across four areas of protection: human health, social assets, biodiversity, and primary production.
milestones.significance: Demonstrated how endpoint monetization translates environmental trade-offs into currency while exposing dependence on population demographics and willingness to pay.

milestones.title: Consolidated ISO 14040:2006 and ISO 14044:2006 Published
milestones.summary: Merged ISO 14041–14043 into a single requirements and guidelines standard (ISO 14044), codifying mandatory critical review and the no-weighting rule for public comparative assertions.
milestones.significance: Remains the foundational global governance benchmark for LCA principles, requirements, and critical review.
milestones.verificationNote: Based on the official public preview clauses of ISO 14040:2006 and ISO 14044:2006 (terms and inventory boundary sections), with comparative-assertion and no-weighting requirements drawn from public guides; the paywalled full texts were not consulted.

milestones.title: UNEP/SETAC Consensus Toxicity Model USEtox Released
milestones.summary: Harmonized European and North American multimedia fate–exposure–effect models into unified comparative toxicity units (CTUh / CTUe) for human toxicity and freshwater ecotoxicity.
milestones.significance: Narrowed multi-order-of-magnitude discrepancies across legacy toxicity models into a transparent, auditable scientific consensus.

milestones.title: ReCiPe 2008 Unifies Midpoint & Endpoint Routes with Cultural Theory Perspectives
milestones.summary: Integrated CML midpoint and Eco-indicator 99 endpoint routes, explicitly parameterizing time horizons and evidentiary thresholds under Individualist (I), Hierarchist (H), and Egalitarian (E) value perspectives.
milestones.significance: Made explicit that endpoint aggregation combines physical cause-effect chains with normative value choices.
milestones.pendingNote: This book directly inspects the ReCiPe 2016 journal article and RIVM report (see the 2016 milestone); the original 2009 ReCiPe 2008 report was not inspected directly and is summarized from subsequent public literature.

milestones.title: European Commission JRC Publishes the ILCD Handbook
milestones.summary: Classified decision contexts into Situations A (micro), B (meso/macro), and C1/C2 (purely descriptive accounting), detailing data quality ratings, compliance blocks, sensitivity checks, and multi-tier review.
milestones.significance: Became Europe's most comprehensive public operational blueprint for life cycle data networks and product footprinting.

milestones.title: GHG Protocol Product Standard, UNEP/SETAC Database Guidance & UK Carrier Bag Study
milestones.summary: GHG Protocol codified corporate single-indicator product carbon footprinting and assurance; UNEP/SETAC issued global LCI database principles; the UK Environment Agency carrier bag study demonstrated how secondary reuse as bin liners governs breakeven thresholds.
milestones.significance: Signaled simultaneous maturation across corporate carbon accounting, global inventory governance, and evidence-based public policy.

milestones.title: Ciroth et al. Empirical Calibration of Pedigree Matrix Uncertainty Factors
milestones.summary: Used empirical resampling of Berlin yogurt cup data to test the correspondence between qualitative pedigree scores and observed data dispersion, replacing purely expert-assigned variances.
milestones.significance: First rigorous empirical challenge to whether qualitative data quality scores can reliably translate into probability variances.

milestones.title: ecoinvent v3 Introduces Multi-System Models & GLO/RoW Residual Architecture
milestones.summary: Separated transforming activities from consumption-mix market activities, offered Cut-off, APOS, and Consequential system models in parallel, and automated GLO-to-RoW residual dataset generation.
milestones.significance: Transformed how modern background databases link processes while making version migration and residual drift central audit concerns.

milestones.title: ReCiPe 2016, AWARE Water Scarcity & UNEP GLAM Particulate Matter Consensus
milestones.summary: Brought watershed-level Available WAter REmaining (AWARE), urban/rural and indoor/outdoor PM2.5 health damage (DALY), and regionalized acidification/eutrophication pathways into mainstream LCIA.
milestones.significance: Moved impact assessment from globally uniform factors to high-resolution, receptor-sensitive spatial characterization.

milestones.title: Danish EPA 15-Indicator Carrier Bag Study Exposes Cross-Category Trade-Offs
milestones.summary: Evaluated unweighted minimum reuse thresholds across 15 indicators for a 22 L / 12 kg shopping trip: organic cotton bags require 149 reuses for climate change alone, but up to 20,000 reuses across all indicators.
milestones.significance: Starkly illustrated how focusing solely on carbon footprint can mask burden shifting into water scarcity, ozone depletion, and land use.

milestones.title: Landmark Reviews Define Red Lines for Uncertainty, Ex-Ante Upscaling & Dynamic Time Horizons
milestones.actor: Heijungs (2020) · Tsoy et al. (2020) · Lueddeckens et al. (2020)
milestones.summary: Heijungs showed Monte Carlo run counts exceeding empirical sample sizes manufacture spurious significance; Tsoy documented a zero-validation gap in ex-ante upscaling; Lueddeckens distinguished assessment, inventory, and characterization time horizons.
milestones.significance: Drew clear methodological boundaries for high-uncertainty comparisons, emerging technology upscaling, and dynamic emission modeling.

milestones.title: EU PEF Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 & Superstructure + IAM Prospective Architecture
milestones.summary: The EU formalized 16 mandatory EF impact categories, the Circular Footprint Formula (CFF), ordinal DQR thresholds, PEFCR-gated comparisons, and A–E performance classes; superstructure databases with scenario difference files (SDFs) streamlined IAM future-background coupling.
milestones.significance: Simultaneously advanced highly standardized regulatory footprinting and resolved computational bottlenecks for 2030/2050 decarbonization scenarios.

milestones.title: EU Batteries Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Embeds Carbon Footprint in Mandatory Market Access
milestones.actor: European Parliament & Council of the European Union
milestones.summary: Established a three-stage mandatory gate (declaration, performance class, maximum legal threshold) for EV, LMT, and >2 kWh industrial batteries, requiring plant-specific data for five core components verified by notified bodies.
milestones.significance: Marked the first major industrial transition of carbon footprinting from voluntary disclosure to legally binding market-access enforcement.

milestones.title: EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) & Prospective LCA Terminology
milestones.summary: ESPR (EU) 2024/1781 extended environmental footprints and Digital Product Passports (DPPs) across physical goods; Arvidsson et al. unified prospective, ex-ante, anticipatory, and dynamic LCA terminology on a two-axis time-position × technology-maturity grid.
milestones.significance: Institutionalized both regulatory compliance infrastructure (DPP) and shared terminology for evaluating emerging technologies.

milestones.title: EU Digital Product Passport Central Registry Milestone & EF 3.1 Secondary Data Transition
milestones.summary: ESPR sets July 2026 for launching the Digital Product Passport central registry, while the European Commission issued EF 3.1 secondary-data transition guidance (projected through 2028) confronting real-world database supply and cross-study comparability tensions.
milestones.significance: Reminds practitioners and regulators that methodological implementation always co-evolves with data supply and version migration—conclusions must remain traceable and revisable.
